documents.title: Academic Honesty Policy
documents.summary: The college-wide Academic Honesty Policy in the Student Handbook is mostly procedure (reporting, hearings, sanctions). Its only AI content is one clause that lists 'unapproved use of artificial intelligence' as a breach of academic integrity on independent work.
documents.stance_why: The one AI clause names 'unapproved use of artificial intelligence' as a violation, so AI is barred unless approved, which is restrict; it does not say who approves or set any tiers.

units.why: The clause lists 'unapproved use of artificial intelligence' among forms of misrepresenting others' work as one's own on independently prepared work. It makes AI use without approval a breach of integrity (actor student, general scope, must-not, P36 because it classifies AI misuse as an integrity violation). P06 was not chosen because it does not say what applies when a syllabus is silent.
units.anchor: unapproved use of artificial intelligence
units.frag_end: resubmitted personal work for another course.
units.policy: Unapproved use of artificial intelligence on projects and assignments prepared independently is an example of academic dishonesty.

documents.title: Computer Science AI Policy Tier System
tiers: Tier 1: See syllabus for allowed usage
Tier 2: Use in any way with required attribution
documents.summary: The Computer Science department sets four tiers of AI use, from none to completely open, and each CS course falls under one tier. It is a pilot for Fall 2026 and the department plans to revisit it regularly. Use outside a course's tier counts as an honor policy violation.
documents.stance_why: The page offers a menu: 'four tiers of allowed use that a course can fall under, from least to most permissive', so the department itself sets no single stance and the choice per course goes to the tier the course adopts; this is delegates with tiers listed.

units.why: States the purpose is 'a unified system' to clarify allowed AI uses 'across all Pomona Computer Science classes'. It is a department-level framework stating purpose and scope, so P56 and informs; P05 is the tier definition itself and is coded separately.
units.anchor: a unified system and increase clarity about what AI usages are allowed or disallowed

units.why: Says the system is a pilot in Fall 2026 and 'we plan to revisit it regularly', which is a commitment to review, so P54 and over-time.
units.anchor: we are piloting in Fall 2026; we plan to revisit it regularly.

units.why: Says the document 'focuses on general usage rather than specific tools' because technology advances rapidly. This sets the scope of what the policy covers (tool-neutral), so P61 and informs.
units.anchor: the document focuses on general usage rather than specific tools

units.why: Defines 'four tiers of allowed use' ordered 'from least to most permissive'. This is the named-tier structure, so P05; the department lets courses choose.
units.anchor: four tiers of allowed use that a course can fall under
units.frag_start: This document outlines the four tiers
units.policy: Each Computer Science course falls under one of four tiers of allowed AI use, from least to most permissive: 0 absolutely no usage, 1 see the syllabus, 2 use in any way with required attribution, 3 completely open use.

units.why: A student whose AI use does not match their course's tier commits a 'violation of our Departmental Academic Honor Policy'. This classes tier breaches as misconduct, so P36 and must-not for students.
units.anchor: it is considered a violation of our Departmental Academic Honor Policy
units.frag_start: If a student uses AI in a way

units.why: Tier 0 says courses 'do not allow the use of any AI'. This is a blanket ban on AI for the course, so P01, must-not, prohibit.
units.anchor: Courses in this tier do not allow the use of any AI.

units.why: Lists disallowed uses 'brainstorm ideas, find source materials, summarize ideas, create study guides, generate code snippets, ... or check your work'. It bans much more than producing submitted work, so the nearest type is P19 with a fit note.
units.anchor: using generative AI tools to brainstorm ideas, find source materials, summarize ideas, create study guides
units.frag_start: Disallowed uses include, but are not limited to
units.fit_note: P19 covers AI producing submitted work; this list also bans brainstorming, finding sources, summarizing, study guides, revising writing and checking work (touching P12, P14, P15, P21).

units.why: Even in Tier 0, 'tools that automatically flag spelling and grammatical errors' such as Word's built-in checker are allowed. It is a narrow permitted writing aid, so P18 and may.
units.anchor: Tools that automatically flag spelling and grammatical errors as you write are allowed

units.why: Tier 0 excludes 'tools that offer suggested revisions of your sentences (for example, Grammarly)'. It is a prose-tool rule, so P18 and must-not.
units.anchor: but not tools that offer suggested revisions of your sentences

units.why: Non-native English speakers 'please ask your instructor' whether translation tools are allowed. Asking before using an unclear tool is P10, and should.
units.anchor: ask your instructor about whether tools for translating words or texts between languages are allowed
units.frag_start: If English is not your first language

units.why: Tier 1 gives 'flexibility for instructors who primarily want to curb AI use but may make exceptions' tailored to course goals. The instructor decides within the tier, so P04.
units.anchor: flexibility for instructors who primarily want to curb AI use but may make exceptions

units.why: Gives the example that a Tier 1 course 'might allow the use of AI for study purposes (e.g., to ask clarifying questions, obtain additional examples, create study guides)' but not on assignments and exams. It names study uses as permitted, so P14.
units.anchor: might allow the use of AI for study purposes (e.g., to ask clarifying questions
units.frag_start: For example, a course following this tier
units.fit_note: Also asks clarifying questions (P12) and bans use during assignments and exams, as an example of what a course may set.

units.why: Students 'must read the course syllabus carefully and discuss allowed uses with their instructor'. This tells students to check and ask rather than assume, so P10 and must.
units.anchor: students must read the course syllabus carefully and discuss allowed uses with their instructor
units.frag_start: Rather than provide an exhaustive list

units.why: Tier 2's goal is 'to openly allow students to use generative AI tools in their learning'. A tier with open permission is P02 and permit.
units.anchor: to openly allow students to use generative AI tools in their learning
units.frag_start: The goal of this policy is

units.why: In Tier 2, if AI plays 'a significant role in the genesis of your work, they should be credited'. This is disclosure with each submission, so P24 and should.
units.anchor: play a significant role in the genesis of your work, they should be credited
units.frag_end: with a collaborating lab partner in a publication.
units.policy: If generative AI tools play a significant role in the genesis of the work, students should credit them in Tier 2 courses.
units.fit_note: Credit is triggered only when AI plays a significant role.

units.why: Credit AI 'in the same way that you would share authorship with a collaborating lab partner'. This is an analogy treating AI like a human collaborator, so P45 and informs.
units.anchor: in the same way that you would share authorship with a collaborating lab partner

units.why: The syllabus 'will contain more information on expectations and attribution formatting' for Tier 2. It says expectations are communicated in the syllabus, nearest P09 with a fit note.
units.anchor: syllabus will contain more information on expectations and attribution formatting.
units.fit_note: Not a requirement on instructors; it states that the syllabus will give expectations and attribution format.

units.why: Tier 3 says 'Students can freely use generative AI tools and do not need to credit their use'. Open use without disclosure is P02, may.
units.anchor: Students can freely use generative AI tools and do not need to credit their use.

units.why: In Tier 3 only, AI-generated text and images 'are treated as the student's own work' under the College policy. No type covers deeming AI output the student's own for integrity purposes, so UNCOVERED.
units.anchor: generated by a student using an AI system are treated as the student's own work
units.frag_start: Specifically and only for classes in Tier 3
units.uncovered_note: In the most open tier, AI-generated text and images count as the student's own work under the College Academic Honesty Policy.

documents.title: Academic Honesty Policy (Computer Science Department)
documents.summary: The Computer Science department Academic Honesty Policy sets general rules for individual work, collaboration, exams, course materials and penalties. Its AI content says AI tools count as unapproved help and refers to the department AI Policy Tier System, which each course follows.
documents.stance_why: The policy says work must not rest on sources 'other than those approved by the instructors, including AI tools' and that 'all Computer Science courses will now follow' the tier system with exceptions 'in the course syllabus'. The actual stance is handed to each course's tier, so delegates.

units.why: Work must be 'completed independently, unless collaboration on a particular assignment is explicitly permitted'. This is a rule that submitted work is the student's own (P29), must. The next sentences apply it to AI.
units.anchor: the work you submit must be completed independently

units.why: Submitted work must not be based on 'information obtained from sources other than those approved by the instructors, including AI tools'. Unapproved sources, AI included, are off limits by default, so P06; P19 is narrower (producing the work).
units.anchor: sources other than those approved by the instructors, including AI tools
units.frag_start: It must not be based on help from others
units.frag_end: approved by the instructors, including AI tools.
units.policy: The work you turn in must not be based on help from others or information from sources other than those approved by the instructors, including AI tools.

units.why: States exceptions 'will appear in the course syllabus or the instructions for an assignment'. This tells where expectations are communicated, P09, informs.
units.anchor: Any exceptions or differences will appear in the course syllabus or the instructions
units.frag_start: Any exceptions or differences will appear
units.fit_note: States that the syllabus or assignment will carry exceptions, rather than requiring it of instructors.

units.why: Says the pilot 'AI Policy Tier System' is one 'that all Computer Science courses will now follow'. Naming a tiered system for all courses is P05.
units.anchor: the Computer Science Department has launched a pilot
units.frag_start: Specifically for the use of Artificial Intelligence
units.policy: Starting in Fall 2026, the Computer Science Department has launched a pilot AI Policy Tier System that all Computer Science courses will now follow.

units.why: AI use that does not align with the course's tier 'is considered a violation of our Departmental Academic Honor Policy'. It classes AI misuse as misconduct, so P36.
units.anchor: it is considered a violation of our Departmental Academic Honor Policy
units.frag_start: If a student uses AI in a way

units.why: 'Ask your instructor if you are ever unsure about what constitutes acceptable behavior.' This is P10, should.
units.anchor: Ask your instructor if you are ever unsure about what constitutes acceptable behavior.

units.why: For individual work, 'Copying solutions from any source, including the web, AI tools, or students ... is not allowed'. AI-made solutions cannot be submitted as one's own, so P19, must-not.
units.anchor: Copying solutions from any source, including the web, AI tools
units.frag_end: of the course, is not allowed.

units.why: States 'We routinely use software and other tools to detect similarities between submissions and generative AI content.' This is use of detection tools, P40, informs.
units.anchor: software and other tools to detect similarities between submissions and generative AI content.

units.why: For papers, 'The prose must be your own', which sets a prose-specific rule separate from code, so P18, must.
units.anchor: The prose must be your own

units.why: External sources 'including AI tools, if permitted, must be properly cited'. This requires acknowledgment of permitted AI use, P24; the prose rule is coded separately as P18.
units.anchor: all external sources, including AI tools, if permitted, must be properly cited

units.why: Students 'should never use course materials or assignments as a prompt for an AI tool, unless explicitly allowed'. Not putting course materials into AI is P49 (P20 also fits; P49 chosen because it names course materials), should-not.
units.anchor: you should never use course materials or assignments as a prompt for an AI tool
units.frag_start: Additionally, you should never use course

units.why: Failure to follow the rules is a violation of 'the College's academic honesty policy', and 'suspected violations are always reported to the Dean of Students Office'. Treating breaches as misconduct with referral is P36.
units.anchor: Suspected violations are always reported to the Dean of Students Office.

units.why: 'A first offense results in a zero and no less than a half-letter-grade reduction.' This states the penalty in advance, P37.
units.anchor: A first offense results in a zero and no less than a half-letter-grade reduction.
units.frag_start: A first offense results in a zero

units.why: A second offense 'is automatically referred to the College's Academic Discipline Board' and the department 'will recommend a failing grade' for a second offense in the same course. Escalating penalties by offense are P37.
units.anchor: A second offense is automatically referred to the College's Academic Discipline Board.
units.frag_start: A second offense is automatically referred
units.policy: A second offense is automatically referred to the College's Academic Discipline Board, and a second offense in the same course leads the Department to recommend a failing grade in the course.

notes: Coded only the three included documents (CS 51, CS 62, CS 105 are deferred). The handbook text is mostly hearing procedure not specific to AI; I coded only its single AI clause. Generic non-AI procedures (evidence standard, appeals) and CS-honesty parts not about AI (group work, exams, TA solutions) were not coded. CS honesty page last revised August 31, 2026.
